analysis: Integration of units 0 and 1: the PR changes only documentation (AGENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md). It adds repository-ownership guidance saying centralized coordinator/backend code belongs in Layr-Labs/darkbloom-platform, and it adds sibling-clone setup instructions. It also labels the coordinator/console directories in this repo as transitional copies. Both analyses agree the docs state that deletion of retained source, hosting changes and deploys are not authorized, and that production deploys still need human approval. No code, config, auth, attestation, encryption, billing, routing or data-flow behavior changes, so nothing touches TB-001/002/005/006/009/011, T-049/T-050 or T-052..T-060 mitigations. AGENTS.md's hop-by-hop encryption description (coordinator decrypts inside its confidential VM, provider is the plaintext endpoint) is consistent with T-003 and A-001. Possible future follow-up, not a defect now: if coordinator code actually moves to darkbloom-platform, threat-model affected_files paths (e.g. coordinator/mediafetch/*, coordinator/api/*) and scope would need re-anchoring, along with security tests and CI. No new attack surface or invalidated assumption was found. Coverage limit: only the docs were reviewed, no code or unchanged callers.
